subject.title: [Feature]: Audit log for agent memory changes

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-class memory mutation audit contract for MEMORY.md and memory/*.md changes, and what integrity, privacy, and cause-propagation model should it use?
rationale: The requested behavior is not a small missing log call; it defines durable memory trust semantics across write surfaces, session context, plugin hooks, storage, and security boundaries.

options.title: Design native memory mutation audit
options.body: Define a SQLite-backed or otherwise integrity-aware memory audit layer with canonical write coverage, actor/session/trigger context, content hash or summary, retention, and focused tests.

options.title: Build durable-write provenance hook first
options.body: Use #48509 and #48519 to define the generic persistence hook/provenance contract, then implement memory mutation audit on top of that seam.

options.title: Defer core audit to plugins for now
options.body: Document the current gap and external prior art while leaving this issue open until maintainers decide whether missing core APIs block a plugin implementation.

recommendation.title: Design native memory mutation audit
recommendation.body: Define a SQLite-backed or otherwise integrity-aware memory audit layer with canonical write coverage, actor/session/trigger context, content hash or summary, retention, and focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/security boundary decision, and steipete appears in recent adjacent memory review context.
